step: Step 4 / KAL-281 — content fingerprints backfilled; storage RE-KEY PREPARED BUT NOT APPLIED

what_was_applied.backfill: YES — applied. content_sha256 written on 87 document rows that had none. This writes ONE column and moves/deletes nothing.
what_was_applied.rekey: NO — deliberately NOT applied. See held_for_human below.
what_was_applied.orphan_deletion: NO — nothing deleted. Listed only, as instructed.

before_after.still_missing_breakdown: 16 fingerprint collisions (identical bytes to another row in the same user+project scope — the script reports and skips these; merging rows moves user marks and is a human decision) + 14 rows whose stored PDF is missing entirely (the dangling rows).

held_for_human.what: rekey --apply would copy 87 objects to their content-addressed path, repoint the rows, and then DELETE the 87 original objects.
why_held: The brief for this run says in plain words: "Do not delete any storage object in this step." Applying rekey deletes 87 production PDFs.
This Supabase project is on the free plan — there is NO point-in-time recovery. A bad delete is permanent.
The owner is switching the app to live payments; the payoff here is cosmetic (storage path naming), so the risk/benefit is poor to take unattended.
Backing the 87 PDFs up to disk first would be ~0.5 GB, which does not belong in the git repo.
held_for_human.safety_work_already_done: Every one of the 87 planned moves was independently verified READ-ONLY: the source object was downloaded and hashed, and its real sha256 matched the row content_sha256 in 87/87 cases. 0 mismatches, 0 missing sources, 0 destinations already occupied. That specifically rules out the KAL-443 fake-fingerprint hazard for this move set — none of the 87 carries a fake fingerprint.
held_for_human.how_to_run_when_approved:
cd <repo> && node scripts/content-hash-maintenance.mjs rekey        # dry-run, re-confirm 87
                             node scripts/content-hash-maintenance.mjs rekey --apply

orphan_warning: Do NOT bulk-delete the 61 orphan objects. KAL-443: the copy-to-project path writes a FAKE fingerprint, so an object can look unreferenced while a row really does depend on it. Each one needs a human eye. Nothing here was deleted.
